result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS (result.status PASS: no applicable invariant fails). Scope test: IN SCOPE, by the secret clause (scripts/seed_meridian_definition.sh is modified and resolves QA_AUTH_TOKEN) and the tenant-data clause (tenant-scoped definition content and tests that write tenant rows). INV-1 APPLIES, PASS. INV-4 APPLIES, PASS. INV-2, INV-3, INV-5, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8, INV-9 and INV-10 are NOT-APPLICABLE: no route, migration, response shaping, lookup-by-ID handler, host function, SQL, outbound URL or permission changed, and lib/ and priv/ have zero changed lines. The refusal body is the fixed constant and the new tests assert it byte-for-byte in all eight refusal assertions. Nothing is loosened: node and edge counts are unchanged, removed lines are version and description only, and the description change is append-only. ESCALATION GAP VERDICT: not a breach of INV-1..INV-10 (it is an in-tenant business separation-of-duties residual; no tenant boundary, secret, response shape, crash or platform authority is involved), and not introduced by this commit (escalate-disburse-loan-to-credit-director had no separation rule before; this commit narrows it). It is a real, verified money-release gap in the QA roster: the single role-credit-director holder can approve at L2 and then release the payment through the escalation if disburse-loan times out. Rated MAJOR for a BA ruling before REQ-465 is marked done. It is not a gate blocker for this step.

evidence.escalation_gap: PATH (all in test/fixtures/qa/meridian_loan_origination_process_definition.json): actor-meridian-julia is the only role-credit-director holder (test/fixtures/uat/actors.yaml:32-35). l2-approval (role-credit-director, distinct_from [l1-approval]) completes, then create-facility, then disburse-loan (role-loan-ops, P1D, distinct_from includes l2-approval). If disburse-loan times out (timeout-disburse-loan, lines 541-542), the flow goes to escalate-disburse-loan-to-credit-director (role-credit-director; distinct_from [l1-approval, escalate-l2-approval-to-ceo, committee-vote-cro, committee-vote-ceo]; l2-approval is NOT named). Its edge e27-escalated goes to end-disbursed, which is the payout. The engine comparison (separation_of_duties.ex, blocking_nodes) only considers named nodes, so the L2 completion is not considered and the completion is accepted. The committee path has the same shape: committee-vote-director (role-credit-director) can vote, then the escalation after a disburse timeout is not refused for the same user. PRE-CHANGE: the escalate node had no separation rule, so the commit narrows the gap for L1, the CEO escalation and the committee CRO and CEO, and does not close it for the two role-credit-director approvers. TESTS: no refusal test exercises escalate-disburse-loan-to-credit-director or ceo-override (grep: only the fixture-shape test names them). The node's own description discloses the open case. CAUSE: the second REQ-464 test in required_outputs_shipped_definitions_test.exs asserts zero single-member candidate pairs across all shipped definitions. That is stricter than REQ-464's acceptance criterion (quoted counts) and than REQ-464's design, where check 4 is a warning that the node could never complete for a single-member role. VERDICT: not an INV-1..INV-10 breach. PASS_WITH_FINDINGS, MAJOR for a BA ruling. Recommended resolution (fail closed): re-add l2-approval and committee-vote-director to escalate-disburse-loan-to-credit-director's distinct_from and relax the zero-pair assertion to REQ-464's membership-aware warning semantics. With one holder, the escalation then has no eligible completer besides the approver and ends at disbursement-held-notice with no payout. Accepting the gap instead needs an explicit BA risk acceptance recorded in REQ-465 that names the L2 approver's self-release; it must not stay implicit. Either path that changes the fixture or the guard needs a new SECURITY-REVIEWER pass.

Pre-existing, not changed by this commit.

issues.description: Escalation residual (result.evidence.escalation_gap). The L2 approver, the sole role-credit-director holder, can release a disbursement through escalate-disburse-loan-to-credit-director after disburse-loan times out. The committee-vote-director can do the same on the committee path. This is an in-tenant separation-of-duties gap, not an INV-1..INV-10 breach. BA ruling required before REQ-465 is marked done: either the fail-closed option (re-add the two pairs and relax the REQ-464 zero-pair test to membership-aware semantics) or a recorded risk acceptance that names this path.

No refusal test covers escalate-disburse-loan-to-credit-director or the regulatory ceo-override node. Both carry distinct_from, and only the fixture-shape test names them. Add refusal tests that match the BA ruling.

Scope question for the BA: no review or memo node is in any distinct_from set. credit-memo-escalation-review (role-credit-director) records credit_decision on the timeout path, and l2-approval (role-credit-director) does not name it, so the same director can record the credit decision and then approve at L2. The REQ scoped adoption to approve, pay and commit nodes, so this is a scope decision, not a defect of this commit.

Transitional rollout gap (result.evidence.rollout): instances created on 1.13 keep their snapshot and no separation rule after the 1.14 activation. The BA or ORCH must accept this or drain in-flight instances.

Drift confirmed (ELIXIR-DEV's note): test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/process_claim_intake.yaml and process_policy_binding.yaml lack distinct_from. The seed script header still calls them the payload sources of truth (scripts/seed_meridian_definition.sh:38-39), but the script deploys test/fixtures/qa JSON (lines 161 and 167). Fix the header or the drift in a follow-up.

Pre-existing, not changed by REQ-465 (for ORCH to decide whether to file per ISSUE_QUEUE): the seed script's default SERVICE_TASK_MOCK_BASE_URL is https://httpbin.org/anything, so seeded QA service-task payloads, including application ids in the disbursement-held-notice path, go to a third-party echo host. Acceptable only for synthetic QA data.
